The motivation for developing our project arises from the growing importance of academic writing quality in technical education.

Students with technical backgrounds are increasingly required to produce research papers, project reports, and theses that adhere to strict formatting standards defined by academic institutions and journals.

While students often possess strong technical knowledge, they frequently lack adequate training in academic writing conventions, resulting in structural and formatting inconsistencies that negatively affect the clarity and professionalism of their work.
A key motivating factor is the limited time available for faculty members to provide detailed formatting feedback.

Professors must manage multiple responsibilities, including teaching, research, and administrative duties, which restricts their ability to thoroughly review formatting aspects of every student submission.
As a result, many formatting errors persist across submissions, slowing students' development of academic writing skills and increasing the overall review burden.
Additionally, existing writing support tools primarily focus on grammar correction and language enhancement, offering minimal assistance for technical formatting issues .
Tools that do address citation management often operate independently and do not verify contextual correctness within the document.
This fragmented support creates a gap in automated academic quality assurance for technical papers.
The need for an affordable and student-friendly automated solution further strengthens the motivation behind this project.
Many available platforms are subscription-based and may not be accessible to all students.

Therefore, a lightweight and specialized platform capable of delivering fast, actionable feedback on technical formatting can significantly improve student productivity, reduce faculty workload, and enhance overall research paper quality.
The domain of academic writing assistance has evolved significantly with the advancement of Natural Language Processing (NLP) and machine learning techniques.
Existing solutions in this area can broadly be categorized into three groups: grammar and language correction tools, plagiarism detection systems, and citation/reference management software.

While these systems contribute to improving academic writing quality, they operate in isolation and do not provide comprehensive structural and formatting compliance verification tailored for technical research papers.
Grammar correction platforms such as Grammarly, LanguageTool, and Writefull utilize NLPbased models trained on large textual corpora to detect grammatical, lexical, and stylistic errors.
Recent research in Grammatical Error Correction (GEC) demonstrates the effectiveness of transformer-based models in improving sentence fluency and readability.
However, these tools primarily treat documents as unstructured text and focus on linguistic refinement rather than academic formatting compliance.
They do not verify figure and table sequencing, caption placement, equation numbering consistency, citation-reference mapping, DOI validation, or journal-specific structural guidelines.
Consequently, while they improve language quality, they fail to address technical formatting requirements essential for engineering research documents.
Plagiarism detection systems compare textual similarity against large academic databases to ensure originality.
These platforms play a critical role in maintaining academic integrity.
However, their objective is limited to similarity detection and originality verification.
They do not analyze structural correctness, formatting consistency, citation integrity, equation referencing, or document layout compliance.
Therefore, plagiarism tools cannot serve as comprehensive academic formatting verification systems.
Reference management tools such as Zotero and Mendeley assist researchers in generating citations in various formats, including IEEE and APA styles.
These tools simplify bibliography creation and reference organization.
Despite their usefulness, they operate as standalone utilities and do not verify contextual correctness within the document.

They do not ensure one-to-one mapping between in-text citations and reference list entries, detect missing references, validate DOI availability, check ordering consistency, or enforce journal-specific formatting constraints across the entire manuscript.

A comprehensive review of existing literature and tools reveals a critical gap: there is no lightweight, integrated system specifically designed to perform structural validation, citation verification, equation compliance checks, figure-table consistency validation, and typography analysis within a single unified platform.
Most available systems focus on isolated aspects of writing improvement rather than holistic academic compliance verification.
This limitation creates the need for an intelligent, automated solution capable of analyzing technical manuscripts as structured academic artifacts rather than plain text documents.
Table 1 presents a structured comparison between existing tools and the proposed system.
The comparative evaluation clearly demonstrates that existing tools operate in silos, addressing either grammar correction, citation generation, or originality verification independently.
None provide an integrated compliance framework capable of analyzing structural formatting, citation integrity, equation consistency, and contextual integration simultaneously.
The proposed system differentiates itself by treating academic manuscripts as structured technical documents.

By combining rule-based validation mechanisms with machine learningbased contextual verification, the system delivers comprehensive, fast, and actionable compliance feedback tailored specifically for engineering and scientific research papers.

Problem Statement Undergraduate and postgraduate students in technical disciplines are required to prepare research papers and project reports that follow strict academic formatting standards prescribed by universities, conferences, and journals.
However, many students lack formal training in technical writing and formatting conventions, which results in frequent structural and stylistic errors in their submissions.

These errors include improper figure and table referencing, missing or incorrectly placed captions, unnumbered or unexplained equations, inconsistent citation styles, and mismatches between in-text citations and the reference list.
The absence of timely and detailed feedback further aggravates the problem.
Faculty members often face a heavy workload and are unable to provide comprehensive formatting corrections for every submission.
As a result, students repeatedly make similar mistakes, leading to poor document quality, increased review cycles, and delays in evaluation or publication.
Existing writing assistance tools primarily focus on grammar and language improvement and offer limited support for technical formatting verification.
Tools that handle citations or references work in isolation and do not validate the overall structural consistency of the document.
Consequently, there is a lack of an integrated, automated solution that can analyze multiple components of a technical paper, including text structure, figures, tables, equations, and references.

Therefore, there is a need for a comprehensive and automated system that can accurately detect formatting inconsistencies, structural errors, and reference-related issues in technical academic documents and provide actionable feedback to help students improve the quality and compliance of their research papers.
The primary objective of our project is to develop an intelligent, automated system capable of verifying the structural and formatting correctness of technical research papers.
The platform is designed to go beyond traditional grammar-checking tools by focusing specifically on academic formatting standards required in engineering and scientific writing.
The purpose of this project is to ensure that research documents comply with institutional and journal-specific guidelines prior to submission.
One of the key objectives is to automatically detect formatting inconsistencies related to figures, tables, and equations.
This includes verifying whether figures and tables are properly numbered, correctly referenced in the text, placed after their first mention, and accompanied by appropriate captions.
For mathematical expressions, the system aims to check sequential equation numbering, proper formatting of variables and units, and whether all symbols are defined clearly within the text.
Another important objective is to validate citation and reference integrity.

The system seeks to ensure that in-text citations correctly correspond to entries in the reference list, that references are complete and properly ordered, and that citation styles such as IEEE or APA are consistently applied.
By automating these checks, the platform reduces the likelihood of submission rejections due to referencing errors.
The project also aims to reduce manual correction effort for both students and faculty members.
By generating structured and actionable feedback reports within a short processing time, the system encourages students to independently refine their work before submission.
This objective directly contributes to improving overall academic writing quality and promoting self-learning.
From a methodological perspective, the system follows a structured processing pipeline.
The process begins when a user uploads a research paper in PDF or DOC format.
The backend then extracts textual content, figures, tables, equations, and references using document parsing utilities.
Following extraction, a rule-based engine employing regular expressions and pattern-matching techniques analyzes structural formatting aspects.
These rules are designed to detect errors such as skipped numbering sequences, incorrect caption placement, improper punctuation, inconsistent typography, and citation bracket formatting issues.
In parallel, machine learning models are applied to analyze the references section more intelligently.
These models assist in identifying incomplete references, mismatches between in-text citations and bibliography entries, DOI validation issues, and inconsistencies in citation style formatting.
The combination of rule-based logic and machine learning enhances both accuracy and contextual understanding.
Finally, the detected issues are aggregated into a structured analysis report.
The report categorizes errors by severity and type, provides specific suggestions for correction, and may include an overall formatting compliance score.
This report is then displayed through an intuitive web interface, allowing users to easily review and implement the suggested improvements.
Through this systematic objective-driven methodology, our project aims to deliver a comprehensive, efficient, and user-friendly solution for technical academic formatting verification.

The simulation platform for the project is designed to replicate a real-world academic document processing environment where research papers are uploaded, analyzed, and evaluated for formatting compliance.
The validation checks implemented in the simulation environment are listed in Table 2.
The backend of the system is implemented using Node.js or Python with FastAPI.
The backend handles core processing tasks, including document parsing, rule-based validation, machine learning inference, and report generation.
FastAPI is particularly suitable due to its high performance, asynchronous capabilities, and compatibility with machine learning workflows.
The backend acts as the central processing unit of the platform, coordinating data extraction, analysis, and structured output generation.
For document analysis and machine learning operations, we have used Python as the primary programming language due to its rich ecosystem of libraries.
Regular expressions and rule-based engines are employed to detect formatting patterns such as figure numbering, citation brackets, equation formatting, and punctuation consistency.
In addition, Natural Language Processing techniques and Scikit-learn models assist in more complex tasks such as citationreference matching, reference completeness verification, and DOI validation.
This hybrid approach ensures both speed and contextual intelligence in error detection.
The system requires a reliable database layer, such as PostgreSQL or MongoDB, to manage user session data, analysis results, and system logs temporarily.
While uploaded documents are not stored permanently in order to maintain privacy, temporary storage ensures smooth report generation and retrieval.
Data deletion policies are implemented to remove documents after processing, ensuring compliance with privacy and academic integrity standards.
From an infrastructure perspective, the platform is deployed on a cloud-based virtual machine capable of handling document uploads and concurrent processing requests.
Containerization using Docker ensures portability and consistent deployment across environments.
Object storage is utilized for temporary file management, while monitoring and logging services maintain system reliability, uptime tracking, and performance diagnostics.
For machine learning model training and experimentation, a short-term GPU-enabled compute instance may be required.
This is particularly useful during development and optimization phases to improve model accuracy in reference classification and pattern recognition.
Once trained, inference can be performed efficiently on standard CPU-based servers to reduce operational costs.
Security and accessibility are also essential requirements of the platform.
A registered do-main name and SSL certificate are necessary to ensure secure HTTPS communication between users and the server.
Authentication mechanisms can be integrated in later stages to support institutional adoption and personalized report tracking.
Overall, the simulation platform integrates modern web technologies, cloud infrastructure, and machine learning frameworks to create a scalable and efficient academic formatting verification system.
The combination of frontend usability, backend computational efficiency, and secure deployment ensures that the system can operate reliably under real-world academic usage conditions.

The proposed system is designed to automatically analyze technical research documents and identify structural, formatting, grammatical, and reference-related issues using a hybrid architecture that combines rule-based validation, regular expressions, Python-based logical checks, Optical Character Recognition (OCR), and machine learning models.
The complete methodology is described below.
The process begins with the user uploading a research paper through a web-based interface.
The system accepts documents in PDF or DOC format.
Once uploaded, the file is securely stored and passed to the backend processing pipeline.
The interface is designed to be intuitive and efficient, enabling rapid submission and automated evaluation.

div.head: OCR-Based Text Extraction and JSON Structuring

p.s: To ensure accurate structural analysis, the system implements an OCR-based processing pipeline for PDF documents.
• The uploaded PDF is first processed using OCR to extract textual and layout information.

• The extracted content is then converted into a structured JSON representation containing hierarchical components such as headings, paragraphs, figures, tables, equations, captions, citations, and references.
• This JSON structure preserves positional metadata (page number, bounding boxes, ordering), enabling precise structural validation.
This intermediate JSON representation serves as the core data structure for downstream validation modules.

div.head: Structural and Formatting Validation Using Regex and Python Checks

p.s: The system applies a rule-based validation engine primarily implemented using:
• Regular Expressions (Regex) The model is trained to recognize structured reference patterns and contextual inconsistencies that cannot be reliably captured using rule-based methods alone.
This makes the reference validation module the most ML-intensive component of the system.
In addition to formatting compliance, the system incorporates grammar and syntax correction.
The integration of grammar validation ensures that the final manuscript satisfies both structural compliance and professional language standards.
The system performs contextual validation to ensure that technical elements are properly integrated within the manuscript.
It verifies:

• Whether every equation is referenced in surrounding text • Whether figures and tables are explained contextually • Whether acronyms are defined at first occurrence This stage moves beyond pattern matching and evaluates semantic integration within the document structure.
After all validations are completed:
• The structured JSON representation is enriched with detected error metadata.
• The system reprocesses the document using OCR-based positional mapping.
• An annotated PDF is generated by overlaying highlights and comments at precise coordinates corresponding to detected violations.
This PDF → JSON → Annotated PDF pipeline ensures traceability between detected issues and their exact visual location in the manuscript.
The system generates a structured compliance report categorizing errors by:
• Category (Figures, Tables, Equations, Citations, References, Typography, Grammar)
• Severity level
The analysis process is optimized for performance and produces results within approximately 40 seconds per document under standard computational settings.

The project "An Intelligent System for Academic Manuscript Formatting and Compliance" has successfully progressed from conceptual design to a fully functional and deployable prototype.

The system is now operational in a real-world environment, with the frontend successfully deployed on Vercel and the backend deployed on Render, ensuring scalability, reliability, and secure cloud-based access.
To validate real-world applicability, the system was rigorously tested on 20 research papers sourced from leading Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs).

The testing phase confirmed that the platform effectively detects structural inconsistencies, citation mismatches, equation formatting issues, figure-table misplacement, and typography errors in technical manuscripts.
The evaluation demonstrated that the system is capable of automatically identifying and reporting formatting violations across all 30 validation checks listed in the simulation framework.

A major milestone achieved during this phase is that the system currently eliminates all grammar and syntax errors identified in the validation table, thereby ensuring that submitted manuscripts meet professional writing standards in addition to structural compliance.
This significantly strengthens the practical reliability of the platform.

Furthermore, the project has received 25,000 rupees in research funding from Netaji Subhas University of Technology (NSUT) to support advanced prototype development, model refinement, and scalability enhancements.
This institutional backing validates both the technical feasibility and academic significance of the system.
The hybrid architecture combining rule-based validation with machine learning models has proven to be highly effective.

Rule-based logic ensures strict adherence to deterministic academic standards (numbering sequences, caption positioning, citation brackets), while machine learning models intelligently validate contextual relationships such as citation-reference map-ping, DOI verification, and reference completeness.
From an infrastructure perspective, successful cloud deployment confirms that the system is production-ready and capable of handling real-time document analysis requests.
The processing time remains optimized at approximately 40 seconds per document, demonstrating both efficiency and scalability.
With continued refinement and expanded dataset validation, the system has strong potential for institutional integration within universities as a mandatory pre-submission compliance tool.
In the long term, the platform can evolve into a standardized academic quality assurance framework capable of improving research submission standards at scale.

Introduction Fix my Paper is a web-based intelligent academic formatting verification platform that is designed to automatically analyze research papers and detect structural, syntactic, citation, and formatting-related errors.
Academic writing in technical domains follows strict formatting standards prescribed by institutions and journals like IEEE, APA etc.
These standards ensure clarity, reproducibility, and professional presentation of research work.
However, undergraduate students often lack formal training in academic writing conventions.

While they may possess strong technical knowledge, they frequently make formatting mistakes such as: • Improper ordering of figures and tables • Missing figure/table captions • Equations without numbering or explanation • Incorrect citation styles • Mismatched in-text citations and reference lists • Inconsistent typography and notation Most of the writing tools that currently exist primarily focus on grammar and language improvement, offering little support for technical formatting compliance.
Fix my Paper helps bridge this gap by integrating rule-based validation and machine learning techniques to generate structured, actionable improvement reports within seconds.
Figure 1: System Architecture of Fix my Paper

Python-based deterministic logical checks Regex-based validation is used for detecting: • Figure and table numbering patterns • Caption placement (above/below validation) • Equation numbering formats • Citation bracket structure (e.g., [1], (1)) • Typography consistency patterns Python logical checks ensure: • Sequential numbering without skipping • One-to-one mapping between mentions and objects • Correct ordering of figures and tables after first reference • Presence of defined symbols and units This rule-driven approach ensures strict compliance with deterministic academic formatting standards.
Machine Learning-Based Citation and Reference Analysis While structural components rely primarily on regex and rule-based checks, reference validation is handled using a machine learning model.

The ML model performs: • Reference completeness verification (authors, title, venue, year, pages) • DOI detection and validation pattern recognition • Citation style classification (IEEE, APA, etc.) • Detection of mismatches between in-text citations and bibliography entries • Identification of incomplete or inconsistent references
This module applies NLP-based correction techniques to detect:

Regex-based rule validation • Python logical checks • Machine learning-based reference intelligence • OCR-based structured reconstruction ensures high precision, contextual reliability, and scalability.
The system is lightweight, cloud-deployable, and cost-effective for students.
It significantly reduces manual formatting effort while minimizing repetitive faculty workload by automating non-conceptual compliance verification tasks.

Technical feasibility through successful cloud deployment • Functional reliability through IIT paper testing • Writing accuracy through grammar and syntax elimination • Institutional validation through research funding support • Scalability ensured through production-ready infrastructure
